details:
ASTRA : Astronaut Health Monitoring Software

Project Overview and How It Works

ASTRA is a prototype health-monitoring dashboard developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026’s challenge, “Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions.” It demonstrates how health-related telemetry, data-quality checks, observations, and mission events can be organized in a single mission-operations interface.

The dashboard visualizes synthetic telemetry across 6-hour, 24-hour, and 72-hour periods, allowing users to review data and compare earlier and more recent sample windows. Its analysis component applies illustrative rules to identify potential observations and data-quality issues. A Mission Event Timeline combines telemetry checkpoints, observations, and simulated communication events to provide chronological context.

ASTRA also demonstrates resilience to communication interruptions. When connectivity is simulated as unavailable, telemetry packets can be queued locally and synchronized when connectivity returns. A read-only integration with NASA’s Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) allows users to search relevant study metadata; it does not download or analyze the studies’ underlying measurements.

Benefits and Intended Impact

ASTRA demonstrates how multiple types of mission health information could be presented in a centralized, understandable interface. Its timeline and comparison features support reviewing changes over time, while data-quality checks help users recognize limitations in the available information. The simulated store-and-forward workflow illustrates how software can preserve queued data during communication interruptions.

The intended impact is to explore a practical software approach to organizing astronaut health-monitoring information, improving situational awareness, and supporting more resilient data handling during space missions. The prototype is educational and experimental: it does not diagnose medical conditions or make flight-operation decisions.

Technology and Development Tools

  • Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI
  • Data handling: Synthetic telemetry, validation rules, local browser storage, and a local JSON L demonstration store
  • Research integration: NASA OSDR study-metadata search
  • Development tools: Node.js, npm, Python, and pytest for backend testing

Creativity and Design Considerations

ASTRA combines several complementary capabilities in one prototype: telemetry visualization, illustrative health observations, data-quality checks, chronological mission-event review, research metadata discovery, and simulated offline queuing and synchronization. Rather than presenting isolated charts, it connects sample measurements and operational events into a more coherent review experience.

The team considered the constraints of space missions, including intermittent communications, the need to understand data quality, clear presentation of time-based information, and the importance of distinguishing real research resources from simulated demonstration data. It also considered scientific validity and safety by labeling the telemetry and thresholds as illustrative rather than medically validated.

ASTRA is a proof of concept, not a NASA-endorsed or flight-certified system. Its current demonstration uses synthetic telemetry and simulated communication events; further work would require validated datasets, expert-reviewed thresholds, stronger security, and rigorous testing before any operational use.
